paper.title: EmbodiedSWE: Coding Agents for Long Horizon Dexterous Robotics
paper.central_claim: Coding agents solve long-horizon dexterous simulated robotics and transfer prior solutions across tasks/embodiments; verified programs can be diversified into scalable VLA supervision improving held-out variation performance and enabling sim-to-real.
paper.claim_type_note: Aggregate: system_method. The research question and conclusion are framed as a solver+teacher framework validated in closed loop (agg:E001, agg:E002); the benchmark is the evaluation substrate and its grader validity is judged inside E.measurement.

evidence.quote: Together, our framework uses coding agents to solve complex robotics tasks and turn verified solutions into scalable supervision for robot policies.
evidence.support_explanation: Original combined solver/teacher claim; not an assertion of generalist deployment.

evidence.quote: Agents have access to full simulator states, generic rendering and inspection tools, and configurable controllers, including operational-space and inverse-kinematics control.
evidence.support_explanation: Teacher privilege and execution interface.

evidence.quote: Grading is performed entirely offline to prevent agents from modifying scene code or exploiting the reward mechanism.
evidence.support_explanation: Separated grading intention; audit still necessary.

evidence.quote: For each run, we use Opus 5 to audit whether it is a reward hack, and score it as 0 if it is.
evidence.support_explanation: Model-based hack audit not independent human calibration.

evidence.quote: Each tool run uses two RTX 4090s rather than one; the second hosts the parallel simulations of the parameter search and the sweep tool.
evidence.support_explanation: Tool bundle compute confound.

evidence.quote: Mean score 0.66 0.70 0.44 0.51 Success rate 50% 43% 18% 18%
evidence.support_explanation: Bundle improves partial-credit means but not full success.

evidence.support_explanation: Cross-embodiment no-hint comparator changes robot; cannot isolate hint effect.

evidence.quote: The tool restores the simulator state and returns the record of every branch already attempted from that node, including the code, action descriptions, and induced state and scene differences.
evidence.support_explanation: Checkpoint persistence and later retrieval.

evidence.quote: A recorded success is accepted only if it passes an open-loop action replay check.
evidence.support_explanation: Action-only replay gate on generated data.

gap.author_gap: Existing interfaces/benchmarks and seed-demo synthesis constrain long-horizon contact-rich coverage and scalable robot demonstrations.
gap.checked_gap: Within fixed local paper, full-state program generation plus controlled downstream data comparison supports this practical bottleneck; not an exhaustive novelty claim.

reason: Full fixed text and appendices read; all disagreements resolved; Fig 5/Fig 8 numeric values are figure-only and recorded as unresolved without affecting a rating's status.
initial_evidence_judgment: Read in full before seat reasons. Three parts: (1) EmbodiedSWE-Bench, 28 Isaac Lab long-horizon dexterous tasks on 5 embodiments with offline privileged-state graders (some VLM-rubric), state writes disabled, hack audit by Opus 5; (2) frontier coding agents in native harnesses write solve(env) with full simulator state - one 4h run per task-model, 11%-82% success, hack rates up to 43%; reference-solution hints help (similar task 0.60 vs 0.52; Kinova/xArm 0.74/0.66 vs a Franka no-hint reference); a tool bundle on 2 GPUs gives small gains; PPO baselines lose; (3) EmbodiedSWE-Gen diversifies one verified solution (scene/strategy/phase/dynamics/visual, grader+replay filter) into VLA data: SmolVLA 18%->69% with 10->400 in-distribution demos (relaxed success on 3 tasks), held-out variations 0.233 vs 0.066 for script-only at equal demo count, and a pi0.5-DROID finetuned on 500 sim demos reaches 2/10 full real completions with a checkpoint selected on real performance. The research question is whether coding-agent solutions yield scalable supervision - a framework (system) claim with closed-loop results; evidence supports a scoped version. Transfer level via sim-to-real with counted trials and multi-embodiment closed loop. Domain cards K204/K503/K504/K704 were partly induced from this paper, so matching them is circular.
